# Cardex

> A single-user Pokémon TCG collection and deck tracker. Static web app (SvelteKit), no server:
> the card catalogue is public JSON on this site; the user's own data lives in their browser
> and, optionally, in one file in their Google Drive.

Live app: https://csicsi2000.github.io/pokemon-card-tracker/
Source: https://github.com/csicsi2000/pokemon-card-tracker

## What an agent can read here (public, no auth)

- /catalogue.json — every English printing (~21k) as compact tuples. Schema in
  src/lib/catalogue-format.ts. Set row: [id, name, series, ptcglCode, releaseDate, cardCount,
  imageBase, symbolUrl, logoUrl, legalStandard, legalExpanded, artworkPublished]. Card row:
  [id, setIndex, localId, name, supertype(P/T/E), subtypes, rarity, regulationMark, hp, types,
  evolvesFrom, variants(n/r/h/f/w), hasImage].
- /details/<setId>.json — attacks, abilities, weaknesses, retreat cost per card of one set.
- Card images: <imageBase>/<localId>/low.webp (or high.webp). Set logos: <logoUrl>.webp.

The user's collection is NOT on this site. It is in their browser's localStorage and, when
they connect sync, in `Cardex/cardex-data.json` in their Google Drive alongside a
human-readable `Cardex/cardex-readable.md`. Read the .md if you have Drive access.

## Formats an agent should speak

Card line (PTCGL / Limitless / pkmn.gg): `<qty> <card name> <SET CODE> <collector number>`
Example decklist the app imports verbatim:

    Pokémon: 4
    4 Charizard ex OBF 125

    Trainer: 4
    4 Arven SVI 166

    Energy: 4
    4 Basic {R} Energy SVE 2

    Total Cards: 12

Quick-add line (no name needed): `MEG 21`, `3 PAL 188 rh` (rh = reverse holo, h = holo).
Set codes are the official PTCGL abbreviations (MEG, OBF, SVI, PAL, SVE, PR-SW …).
Deck requirements count by card NAME: any printing the user owns satisfies a line.

## URLs an agent can hand to the user

- /import/?list=<url-encoded decklist>  — opens the importer pre-filled for review
- /import/?list=…&target=deck&name=<deck name>  — same, preselecting "new deck"
- /cards/?q=<name>  — browse; /cards/?set=<setId>  — one set

## Tools for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI)

In a checkout of the repo:
- `npm run cardex -- help`  — CLI over a data file (a backup export, or the Drive-mirrored
  cardex-data.json). Read collection/decks, create and edit decks, quick-add cards, buylists.
- `npm run mcp`  — the same operations as an MCP server over stdio (CARDEX_DATA=path).
See AGENTS.md and docs/deck-coach-prompt.md in the repository.
